evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by images in Figure 7.

claim: ActGSI-3 cells grow as floating cell clumps that may recapitulate subepidermal clusters of sessile hemocytes of the larva (Leitão and Sucena, 2015; Márkus et al., 2009).
source: The cells grow as floating cell clumps (Figures 1 and 7) that may recapitulate subepidermal clusters of sessile hemocytes of the larva (Leitão and Sucena, 2015; Márkus et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citations and supported by images in Figures 1 and 7.

claim: The most significantly upregulated marker genes in each cell line are significantly enriched for top marker genes from expected cell types based on the single-cell RNAseq data from Fly Cell Atlas in most cases.
source: The most significantly upregulated marker genes in each cell line are significantly enriched for top marker genes from expected cell types based on the single-cell RNAseq data from Fly Cell Atlas in most cases.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a summary of the RNAseq analysis results.

claim: Some cells in the mesodermal clone, 24B5-B8, are positive for HRP (Figure 5—figure supplement 1; Supplementary file 2).
source: For example, some cells in the mesodermal clone, 24B5-B8, are positive for HRP (Figure 5—figure supplement 1; Supplementary file 2)
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an example of anomalous gene expression and supported by images in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: The two neuronal-like lines express a mesodermal marker, Twist (Figure 6—figure supplement 2; Supplementary file 2).
source: and the two neuronal-like lines express a mesodermal marker, Twist (Figure 6—figure supplement 2; Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an example of anomalous gene expression and supported by images in Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: This anomalous gene expression is likely to be an effect of Ras activation on downstream pathways and genes.
source: This anomalous gene expression is likely to be an effect of Ras activation on downstream pathways and genes.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an interpretation of the anomalous gene expression.

claim: Ras/MAPK has a key role in muscle cell determination (Buff et al., 1998; Carmena et al., 2002; Halfon et al., 2000).
source: Ras/MAPK has a key role in muscle cell determination (Buff et al., 1998; Carmena et al., 2002; Halfon et al., 2000) and activates downstream muscle determination genes.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citations to support the known role of Ras/MAPK.

claim: Glial cell missing (gcm) is not differentially expressed in the three glial-lineage cell clones.
source: It will also be important to consider what genes are not expressed by a given cell line, for example, glial cell missing (gcm) is not differentially expressed in the three glial-lineage cell clones
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an observation about gene expression patterns.

claim: gcm2 is differentially expressed in only two of the three glial-lineage cell clones.
source: and gcm2 is differentially expressed in only two of the three clones.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an observation about gene expression patterns.

claim: Trachealess (trh) is only differentially expressed in one of the three tracheal-lineage cell lines.
source: Further, trachealess (trh) is only differentially expressed in one of the three tracheal-lineage cell lines.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an observation about gene expression patterns.

claim: The muscle-specific transcription factors twist (twi), nautilus (nau), snail (sna), and Mef2 show variable expression in the muscle-lineage cell clones.
source: Similarly, the muscle-specific transcription factors twist (twi), nautilus (nau), snail (sna), and Mef2 show variable expression in the muscle-lineage cell clones.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an observation about gene expression patterns.

claim: The cells will have value for both low- and high-throughput approaches, including genetic or compound screens.
source: The cells will have value for both low- and high-throughput approaches, including genetic or compound screens for which screening in the relevant cell type will result in identifying targets that are more likely to be of physiological relevance.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a potential application.

claim: Most of the cells have an attP-flanked cassette (Table 1), which makes them amenable to insertion of transgenes such as reporters by Recombination Mediated Cassette Exchange (RMCE) (Bateman et al., 2006; Manivannan et al., 2015).
source: Most of the cells have an attP-flanked cassette (Table 1), which makes them amenable to insertion of transgenes such as reporters by Recombination Mediated Cassette Exchange (RMCE) (Bateman et al., 2006; Manivannan et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citations and supported by data in Table 1.

claim: Cells competent for RMCE can be modified by stable expression of Cas9 and then used for genome-wide CRISPR pooled screening.
source: Moreover, cells competent for RMCE can be modified by stable expression of Cas9 and then used for genome-wide CRISPR pooled screening.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a potential application.

claim: To date, pooled CRISPR screens in Drosophila have only been performed in S2 cells, which have hemocyte-like features.
source: To date, pooled CRISPR screens in Drosophila have only been performed in S2 cells, which have hemocyte-like features.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as background information.

claim: The availability of new cell lines with muscle, glial, and epithelial characteristics will enable screens designed to interrogate biological processes specific to these cell types.
source: The availability of new cell lines with muscle, glial, and epithelial characteristics will enable screens designed to interrogate biological processes specific to these cell types.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a potential application.

claim: The number of Drosophila cell lines corresponding to known cell types is low.
source: There are hundreds of Drosophila cell lines; however, the number corresponding to known cell types is low.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as background information.

claim: The lack of a method for generating cell lines from specific tissues has contributed to the low number of cell lines corresponding to known cell types.
source: This is due in part to the lack of a method for generating cell lines from specific tissues.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an explanation for the low number of characterized cell lines.

claim: The method using restricted expression of RasV12 is expected to be a tractable approach for investigators to generate lines of cell types of interest.
source: We expect that the method described here, using restricted expression of RasV12, will be a tractable approach for investigators to generate lines of cell types of interest.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a conclusion about the utility of the method.

claim: Single-cell cloning followed by cell characterization (immunohistochemistry and RNAseq) proved to be a useful method to identify cell-type-specific lines.
source: Single-cell cloning followed by cell characterization (immunohistochemistry and RNAseq) also proved to be a useful method to identify cell-type-specific lines and this approach could identify additional valuable lines in the existing collection at the DGRC.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a conclusion about the utility of the cloning approach.

claim: Lineage-restricted Ras expression and cell cloning has produced a set of new cell lines that will be of immediate value for analyses in the five cell types they represent.
source: In summary, we show that lineage-restricted Ras expression and cell cloning has produced a set of new cell lines that will be of immediate value for analyses in the five cell types they represent.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a summary conclusion.

claim: All cell lines described have been deposited to the Drosophila Genomics Resource Center (DGRC) at Indiana University.
source: All cell lines described here have been deposited to the Drosophila Genomics Resource Center (DGRC) at Indiana University.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials availability section.

claim: The lines are available for distribution to the research community.
source: The lines are available for distribution to the research community.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials availability section.

claim: The dataset (Ras cell lines) has been imported into the Drosophila Gene Expression Tool (DGET) database (https://www.flyrnai.org/tools/dget/web/), which is the bulk RNAseq data portal at Drosophila RNAi Screening Center (DRSC) (Hu et al., 2017).
source: The dataset (Ras cell lines) has been imported into the Drosophila Gene Expression Tool (DGET) database (https://www.flyrnai.org/tools/dget/web/), which is the bulk RNAseq data portal at Drosophila RNAi Screening Center (DRSC) (Hu et al., 2017).
